To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

discrete torsion can always be gauged away, that a large class of generalized discrete torsion is equivalent to changing Wilson lines, and that a large class (possibly all?) of generalized discrete torsions can be obtained by changing the compactification lattice.

1. The discrete torsion phase can be gauged away by changing shifts by lattice vectors; 2. A large class of the generalized discrete torsion phase, can be gaugeded away by changing background fields by lattice vectors; and

discrete and generalized discrete torsion in heterotic orbifold models can be traded for changes in the compactification lattice and Wilson line moduli, and that the latter can be used to trade models with discrete torsions for torsionless models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the classification of heterotic string compactifications on Z_NxZ_N orbifolds with discrete torsion.
the study of heterotic Z_N x Z_M orbifolds with discrete torsion.
the classification of heterotic Z_N x Z_M orbifold models with discrete torsions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of inequivalent heterotic Z_N x Z_M models is equal to the number of inequivlaent Z_N x Z_1 orbifolds.
discrete torsion is not a fundamental concept in string theory.
the discrete torsion is a gauge artifact, and that it does not affect the physical properties of the theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heterotic Z_N x Z_M orbifolds can be classified by the gauge embedding, the compactification lattice and the background fields.
the heterotic discrete torsion is not a fundamental ingredient, but is rather a consequence of certain choices for the lattice shifts, Wilson lines and/or compactification lattice.
all the discrete torsion phases are either trivial or are related to the Wilson lines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the classification of heterotic orbifolds is not as simple as it seems at first sight.
discrete torsion is a gauge artifact.
the discrete torsion phase is not a fundamental feature of the theory, rather it can be traded for a change of the background fields.
